The searchable copy is a denormalized SQLite table, maintained by in-process event listeners. For a title edit, [issue-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6ab21918-b744-4f66-bd88-1697b5314b39/src/server/services/issue-service.ts) runs `updateIssue`: it checks organization scope, loads the issue, checks `issue:update` and that the issue is not archived, then calls `issueRepo.updateIssue`. After the write, it awaits `emit("issue.updated", ...)`.

At server startup, `registerEventHandlers` in [event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6ab21918-b744-4f66-bd88-1697b5314b39/src/server/services/event-registry.ts) calls `registerSearchListeners` in [search-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6ab21918-b744-4f66-bd88-1697b5314b39/src/server/services/search-service.ts). The `issue.updated` listener re-reads the issue by organization and ID, then calls `indexIssue`, which calls `upsertSearchDocument`. Thus the listener indexes the saved row rather than relying on the event’s changed-fields list. [event-bus.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6ab21918-b744-4f66-bd88-1697b5314b39/src/lib/event-bus.ts) waits for all subscribers to settle, so a successful indexing handler normally finishes before `updateIssue` returns. Handler failures are reported to error sinks and are not rethrown, however: the ordinary write can succeed while the index remains stale.

The same listeners index created issues and comments, remove archived issues and deleted comments, and index created projects or remove archived projects. A `search.reindex_requested` listener re-reads and indexes an issue; it ignores other subject kinds. For recovery after bulk import or drift, `runSearchReindexJob` in [search-reindex-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6ab21918-b744-4f66-bd88-1697b5314b39/src/server/jobs/search-reindex-job.ts) re-upserts projects, issues and their live comments. Its current implementation requests one page of up to 100 at each level; it does not follow subsequent cursors or remove stale documents.

The `searchIndex` table in [webhooks.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6ab21918-b744-4f66-bd88-1697b5314b39/src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts) stores an ID, organization ID, subject kind and ID, optional project ID, content and indexing timestamp. `indexIssue` stores the title followed by the description; `indexComment` stores the body with no project ID; `indexProject` stores name followed by description and uses the project’s ID. `upsertSearchDocument` in [search-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6ab21918-b744-4f66-bd88-1697b5314b39/src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts) finds a document by organization, kind and subject ID, then updates its content, project and timestamp or inserts it.

For a search through the dialog, `SearchDialog` in [search-dialog.tsx](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6ab21918-b744-4f66-bd88-1697b5314b39/src/components/domain/search/search-dialog.tsx) debounces the input and calls `parseSearchQuery` in [query-syntax.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6ab21918-b744-4f66-bd88-1697b5314b39/src/components/domain/search/query-syntax.ts). With advanced search enabled, the parser removes recognized `kind:`, `in:` and `project:` tokens into filters, reports unknown tokens as ignored, and sends the remaining text to `onSearch`. Without it, the entire trimmed input is treated as text. The dialog does not send an empty remaining query.

For the server-action path, `searchAction` in [search.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6ab21918-b744-4f66-bd88-1697b5314b39/src/actions/search/search.ts) uses `withAction` to validate against `searchQuerySchema`, resolve the actor and translate errors into an `ActionResult`. The schema in [search.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6ab21918-b744-4f66-bd88-1697b5314b39/src/schemas/search.ts) requires a query of 1–200 characters and defaults kinds to issues. The action checks `org:read`, loads the organization’s flag context, and, when `advanced_search` is off, filters requested kinds down to issues before calling the service. The separate `GET` endpoint in [route.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/6ab21918-b744-4f66-bd88-1697b5314b39/src/app/api/search/route.ts) resolves the actor from `orgSlug`, checks `org:read` and `command_palette`, validates the query, and calls the same service; it returns items and total as JSON.

`search` in `search-service.ts` then checks actor organization scope and organization-level `issue:read`, consumes an organization-wide `search:query` token, loads the organization and evaluates `advanced_search`. It refuses a query containing **any colon** when that flag is off—even a literal colon in an otherwise valid title search, despite the client parser treating it as plain text. It also refuses a request when the token bucket is exhausted, and authorization, authentication, schema validation or the palette flag can reject it earlier. With the flag on, server-side search does not itself parse field syntax; the dialog’s parser supplies the filters.

Finally, `searchDocuments` applies the organization predicate, a SQL `LIKE` substring match on content, optional kind and project filters, counts matches, and fetches a cursor page ordered by newest `indexedAt` and ID. `search` converts each row to a `SearchHit`: its first content line becomes the title, `snippetAround` extracts context around the query, and `hrefFor` builds the subject link. The action returns the items; the JSON endpoint also returns the total. One detail of the repository filter is that an **empty** kinds array means no kind restriction, so an action request narrowed from only non-issue kinds to an empty array is not restricted to issues by `searchDocuments`.
